opportunities.query_text: Uber burned its entire 2026 AI budget in four months, and had to cut back on usage. Agentic AI cost just doesn't behave like traditional software that we know how to budget for. I spent years at Apptio building the tooling that made cloud spend predictable, and that playbook doesn't survive contact with agents. Most teams are learning that lesson the hard way. My new piece is on why agentic AI keeps blowing out of budget, and what makes it so hard to see coming. Would like to hear from others how they are managing their AI costs.

opportunities.query_text: Amplemarket wants to replace your SDR stack with one AI copilot... I publish tool reviews on marketintelligencetools.com, and I just finished a long one on Amplemarket... I want to hear from people who've run real pipeline through it, especially anyone who came from Apollo, Outreach or Salesloft and can compare the switch directly. Amplemarket bundles a 200-million-contact database, outreach across seven channels and an AI copilot called Duo into one contract. The Startup plan is $600 a month for two seats, billed annually, with no monthly option and no published free trial anywhere on the site. Fifteen thousand email credits and 480 phone credits per user come with it, plus two mailboxes. Growth and Elite are both custom quotes, & neither publishes a number. Vendr's tracked-contract data puts the real median at $16,608 a year, ranging from $11,678 to $35,946. That's two to five times the advertised Startup rate, once a team needs the tiers Amplemarket won't price in public. Has anyone here signed a Growth or Elite contract? I'd like to know if the number landed near that $16,608 median, or somewhere past the $35,946 high end Vendr has on record?

The strongest remains the FinOps agentic-AI-cost-overrun request (#1) — the core AIToolsEssentials problem, now on its fourth consecutive appearance with no refresh in five days, which reads as a closing window rather than an open one. The best new find is the Amplemarket pricing review (#2): a reviewer refusing to accept published pricing, pulling Vendr's tracked-contract median ($16,608/yr against a $600/mo advertised Startup tier), and asking for signed-contract data points — the most methodologically aligned request this monitor has seen, and the natural fit for AIToolsEssentials' verified-pricing discipline. The freshest is the Anthropic customer service story (#3), under 24 hours old, which turns a support complaint into the value question buyers actually face at $200/month tiers. The enterprise agent-sprawl request (#4) stays live and still names cost visibility explicitly. Science Magazine (#5) is now eight days old with no refresh and should be treated as a late data offer, not a live placement. Two items carried into this run were retired correctly and one was not: the Forbes 2027 tech-budgets request is back on the Forbes page today after being reported as rotated off yesterday, which exposed a real methodological error in this monitor — Sourcee outlet pages are persistent ~20-item lists (the TechCrunch page still carries a request dated 2025-09-12), so absence from an outlet page is not evidence of expiry. The 2026-09-11 retirements of the Forbes and FT items were made on that faulty test and are corrected or softened here. Access did not improve: HARO and Connectively now both sit behind a Vercel Security Checkpoint returning HTTP 429 (the gate changed vendor, not strength), Qwoted needs an authenticated app session, MentionMatch still serves an empty pre-launch shell, Source of Sources has no query feed at all, and X search is out of credits for the fourth consecutive run. monitor_health.extraction_fix_this_run: Sourcee request pages stopped serving an HTML <main> element and now render as a Next.js App Router page. The request text lives in an RSC flight payload as a JSON-LD Article object: headline, description, datePublished. New recipe — curl with a browser UA, then regex the escaped JSON-LD fields: re.search(r'\\"description\\":\\"((?:[^"\\\\]|\\\\.)*?)\\"', raw). The old recipe (strip tags from <main>) returns 0 characters on every request page and fails silently. A companion trap: the string 'has disappeared faster than a leaked story' is present in the bundled 404 component on EVERY page including valid ones — do not use it as a removal test, it produces false 'removed' verdicts. Author names are NOT reliably extractable (the JSON-LD name field returns CSS hint strings like 'next-size-adjust'); use the headline as the title and treat the author as unknown.
monitor_health.outlet_page_fix_this_run: Outlet pages (/media-outlets/<slug>/journo-requests) render ~20 persistent listings, not a rolling newest-first feed — Forbes carries a listing dated 2026-07-20 and TechCrunch one dated 2025-09-12. Absence from an outlet page is not evidence that a request expired. Withdraw an item only after two consecutive absences or a stated deadline passing.
